$comment: Pins the owner decision of 2026-11-06 on #176 item 18: `accepted_identity_types` is open. The body is man-005's without `extensions`, plus `accepted_identity_types: ["oidc", "x509"]`, so the unrecognised entry is the only thing under test. `x509` is a Reserved row of registries/identity-types.md that no `aitp/0.3` implementation implements. That is the realistic case: a type specified later, listed by a publisher that implements it, read by a verifier that does not. Before RC2.1 every verifier returned MANIFEST_INVALID for this Manifest, because the schema closed the list to `oidc`, `pinned_key` and `spiffe`.
description: Manifest whose `accepted_identity_types` lists a type the verifier does not implement (`x509`) beside one it does (`oidc`). RFC-AITP-0003 §3.2: the list is open, so the unrecognised entry is inside the grammar and does not make the Manifest MANIFEST_INVALID at §5 step 2; at §5 step 6 the verifier ignores it. Version, expiry, PoP and signature all pass, so the Manifest verifies.

expected.rationale: The Manifest is schema-valid: an `accepted_identity_types` entry is any non-empty string. Version, expiry, proof-of-possession and signature pass, and the signing input covers `accepted_identity_types` as written, unrecognised entry included (RFC-AITP-0003 §6.1). `verify_manifest` runs no fetcher-side screen, and the unrecognised entry would not change that screen's outcome: it is ignored, and `oidc` is still listed (RFC-AITP-0003 §5 step 6).
